Fun Facts[]

  • This station was originally planned to be a single-line station for Akashi Line and did not involve Urban Line. However, later considerations had seen that Passengers who travelled on Akashi Line and Daybreaker Line would have to go to Mei Fwong Station before they could get access to Urban Line and the rest of the Nazca Railway network, which involved large degrees of detours. As a result, it was decided that this station would be inserted onto Urban Line. However, it should also be noted that this rule did not apply for passengers from Old Brightland Station as The Shuttle and Southern Corridor of Nawis Railway were already available at the time.[2]
  • This station is the fourth station to be inserted between two existing stations, with the first three inserted stations being Metro Stone Station, Kamelen Station and Twenty Village Station.
  • In order to enable opposite-direction transfers between Urban Line and Akashi Line, Akashi Line temporarily took the right-hand traffic rule, where trains travel on the right side of the tracks instead of the left. This arrangement is similar to Sava Line switching travelling directions at Horsepower Island Station in the same episode.
  • The name of this station alludes to a Battle Sprite of the Same Name in Spiral Knights.[3]

History[]

  • August 22 2020: This station began services. Urban Line trains began stopping at this station, and Akashi Line extends from Myosotis Valley Station to this station.
  • June 16 2021: Platform signs have been upgraded for Akashi Line, revealing the plans for Akashi Line Phase 3 between Python Delta Station and Summer Point Gateway.[4]

  • April 8 2021: This stop began construction.

Fun Facts[]

  • This station features the first set of "Inter-railway, Cross-Platform" interchange platforms in Nazca Railway.
  • Lei Wah Depot, the depot for Cometsilk Line, is located next to this station.

History[]

  • March 31 2019: This station completed construction.[2] At the same day, this station began services alongside StarTop Railway Cadence Line.
  • April 3 2019: Cometsilk Line extended from Waterbelt Garden Station to this station.
  • June 2 2019: Cometsilk Line Harvest River branch began services. Cometsilk Line extended from Waterbelt Garden Station and this station to Harvest River Station.
  • September 30 2020: This station is chosen by NR as the background picture for the mid-autumn festival of that year.[3]

Station Title and Soundtrack[]

  • The Station Title of this Station is Cryoclast Spire.
  • This Station features two soundtracks that belong to the album "Where Cold Order Moves and Night Becomes String".
Name of the Soundtrack Length (mm:ss)
Cryoclast Spire 03:14

Fun Facts[]

  • This Station is the first Single Line Station of Ingress Line to be built since its establishment on April 13 2017.
  • This station , alongside Silvane Station and Lake Winter Station are considered "Sister Stations" with similar design, and extra open platform spaces are seen at both ends of the platforms; Therefore, the actual length of the platforms in this station is 264m.
  • This Station is named after the Ice Spikes biome to the north of this station that resembles Ice Pillars. While a Similar Biome can also be seen to the north of Spike End Station, they can't be seen from the station itself as Spike End Station is an underground Station. However, the Ice Spikes are visible from Platform 1 of this Station.
  • A Corroded Cave exists to the southeast of this station in a fashion similar to Barode Cave Station. As a result, the road to the south of this station avoids that cave.
  • A Staff-only Passageway exists between the Central Transfer Passageway and the East Transfer Passageway.

History[]

  • September 5 2025: This Station began construction.
  • September 6 2025: This Station completed construction.
  • September 7 2025: This Station began services.

Fun Facts[]

  • The color scheme and the Chinese Name of this station alludes to Tsim Sha Tsui Station of the MTR in Hong Kong. Moreover, as "Tsim Sha Tsui" means "Sharp Spit" in Cantonese, the name Sharp Spit is adopted for this station as a sharp spit also exists near this station at the time of its construction.[2]
  • In order to allude to Tsim Sha Tsui Station in Hong Kong, a clock tower resembling the Clock Tower in Hong Kong is constructed outside this station.

History[]

Shatterpass Station is a station on New Edward Line. It is operated by Nazca Railway (Los Sengas Division), and is located at Los Sengas Cometsilk.

Fun Facts[]

  • The English Name of this station has hinted that the Current Chinese Name of this station before beautification.[4]
  • A New variant of the Elevated Bridge exists between Nail Bight Checkpoint and this station.
  • The First Chinese Word of this station refers to small and shattered pieces of silk. This not only alludes to the original name of this station, but also alludes to the District Theme of Cometsilk.
  • The Design of this station references Dul-las Station, with an underground concourse connecting to the exit on the road next to the station body. However, unlike Dul-las Station, the Concourse of this station extends to beneath the road as well.[5]

History[]

  • January 31 2022: This Station completed construction.[6]
  • February 1 2022: New Edward Line extended from Nail Bight Checkpoint to Hillfield Station through this station.

Fun Facts[]

  • The name of this station, as well as this area of the Tin Kum-Shek Pai Tau New Town, is named after the Shek Pai Tau Road in Hong Kong, which in turn is named after what is now the Tuen Mun Industrial Area.[2]
  • While the official floor guide of this station denotes the Concourse as Level B1, as it is situated at Y=66, and some of the Exits (Exits A, D) of this station are already at ground level, it is denoted at LG on this page.
  • While this station is situated at the east end of what is now the Tin Kum-Shek Pai Tau New Town today, the term Shek Pai Tau in this station used to refer to the entire New Town Area at the time this station was built.

History[]

  • June 14 2020: This Station completed construction.[3] At the same day, this station began services.

Fun Facts[]

  • This station is named after a group of an orientation camp which became a champion in which the railway builder participated in.[2] However, the name of that group in turn alludes to the YOKOHAMA Tires commercial in which Louis Koo, a Hong Kong-based actor, mispronounced several Mandarin words and made them sound like profanities in Cantonese. This incident has since become an Internet Meme in Hong Kong.[3]
  • The Platform type of this station is unique. The platforms of this station could not be seen as traditional island platforms as each section of the platform only enables trains to stop at one side only, with the other side being a wall at both sections. On the other hand, as both sections of the platform are accessible from each other on foot, the platforms could not be seen as side platforms either. As a result, this station could be seen as having "Slanted Island Platforms". A similar platform layout could be seen at Info Island Hospital Station of the Info Island Railway.
  • The Kinight Line Platforms of this station have been sealed off for five years and four months before it began services at this station.[4]

History[]

  • September 22 2015: This station began services alongside West Ring Line. Kinight Line Platforms are already reserved, but is sealed off from public access.
  • August 15 2016: This station finished Upgrading Works.[5]
  • June 21 2018: This station finished Second Stage Upgrading Works.[6]
  • February 3 2021: The concourse of this station completed expansion, and the Kinight Line platforms have been opened to the public. However, the Kinight Line platforms have yet to begin services.
  • February 18 2021: Kinight Line extends from Darey Terrace Station to this station.
  • March 23 2023: The Station Title Banner of this station is added.
  • September 1 2023: The Station Banners of this station are set up.
  • December 23 2024: This station completed its Station Title and Icon Upgrade Scheme.[7]

Sheung Che Nung Stop is a stop of Sheung Yam Line and Tsing Lam Line. It is operated by Nazca Railway Sexterade LRT, and is located at Los Sengas Twenty-Second Continent. Passengers may also use this station to change to Nazca Railway West Ring Line, Kinight Line (Sheung Che Nung Station), Akashi Line (Red Millet Station) and Nawis Railway Masquerade Line (Halozy Station).

History[]

Shizuoka Street Stop is a station of SLT Line 104. It is located between Downtown and Sava within Los Sengas. Passengers may also use this station to change to Great City Railway Lakebound Line (Shizuoka Street SLT Station).

  • Although this station is close to Nazca Railway Phoenix Line (Bonyal North Station), there are no connecting pathways between them.
  • Although this station is at the boundary between Los Sengas Downtown and Sava, this station belongs to Fare Zone 1.

title: Shore Tip LRT
safeHtml:
Shore Tip Local Rapid Transit, abbreviated as Shore Tip LRT, is a Local Rapid Transit System of NR Los Sengas Division.

Contents

  • 1 Concept
  • 2 List of Lines
  • 3 Fun Facts
  • 4 See Also
  • 5 Citations and References

Concept[]

Shore Tip LRT mainly serves the Shore Tip Area in Internal Sea, with plans to extend to Bowplate River in the future.

List of Lines[]

  • 1 Tung Wik Line
  • 2 Ting Wik Line

Fun Facts[]

  • The Platform Building Material of Shore Tip LRT was formerly Green Concrete. However, after the establishment of Peckern North LRT, Green Concrete was replaced by Cyan Concrete to avoid conflicts.

See Also[]
